rv.q: This World Premiere of Bo List’s new adaptation of R.U.R. is a robust reboot.
Brian Pastor and the creative crew do an excellent job of bringing this century-old human story to life without making it seem silly.
The conceptual humor had me laughing frequently.

City Lit's production cleverly uploads modern technology into Čapek's work, changing the elusive 'magic substance' that brings robots to life with the real-life mystery of the inner workings of the 'black box' that comprises AI reasoning.
There are two major reasons why I can’t recommend this show.
Costuming by Beth Laske-Miller is exceptional and visually “futuristic” by showing great restraint and keeping within the range of the naivety of the play’s overall attitude.
It is also funny, creative, and thought-provoking.
This is a prescient story that is more relevant today than ever!

cn.t: This freely adapted world premiere of Čapek's 1920 sci-fi classic earns mostly positive reviews for its timely AI themes and humor, though one critic finds the lighter tone undermines the original's darker warnings about automation and humanity.
